original_question: Is it consistent that the splitting number equals the continuum and both are larger than ℵ2, while for every κ in [ℵ1, c]—including κ = s itself—the strong polarized relation \( inom{\kappa}{\omega} 	o  inom{\kappa}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) holds?
target_in_paper: Problem 3.14 in §3: whether it is consistent that the splitting number s equals the continuum c, that s = c > ℵ2, and that \(\binom{\kappa}{\omega} \to \binom{\kappa}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) for every cardinal \(\kappa \in [\aleph_1, c]\), explicitly including \(\kappa = s\) itself. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s official formulation: it has the right cardinal characteristics (s and c), the right size demand \(s=c>\aleph_2\), the right universal quantifier over cardinals between \(\aleph_1\) and \(c\), and the paper’s own emphasis that the endpoint \(\kappa=s\) is the extra case of interest. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
missing_details: Define the strong polarized relation explicitly: for every coloring \(c:\kappa\times\omega\to 2\), there exist \(A\subseteq\kappa\) and \(B\subseteq\omega\) with \(|A|=\kappa\) and \(|B|=\omega\) such that \(c\restriction(A\times B)\) is constant. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))

State that \(\kappa\) ranges over cardinals, and identify \(s\) as the splitting number and \(c\) as the continuum \(2^{\aleph_0}\); the paper states the interval as \(\kappa\in[\aleph_1,c]\). ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))

Phrase it overtly as a ZFC consistency question (equivalently: asking for a model/forcing extension of set theory with these properties), since the paper’s official wording is 'Is it consistent that ... ?' ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))

For paper-faithful context, note why the endpoint matters: by Theorem 2.6, if \(\kappa<s\) and \(\operatorname{cf}(\kappa)>\aleph_0\), then \(\binom{\kappa}{\omega}\to\binom{\kappa}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) already holds; thus under \(s=c<\aleph_\omega\), the genuinely new issue is whether the relation can also hold at \(\kappa=s\). ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))

Include the nearby hidden restriction noted by the paper: any positive answer must in fact have \(c<\aleph_\omega\), since \(\binom{\aleph_\omega}{\omega}\nrightarrow\binom{\aleph_\omega}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\). ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
refined_question: Is it consistent with ZFC that the splitting number \(\mathfrak{s}\) equals the continuum \(\mathfrak{c}=2^{\aleph_0}\), that \(\mathfrak{s}=\mathfrak{c}>\aleph_2\), and that for every cardinal \(\kappa\) with \(\aleph_1\le \kappa\le \mathfrak{c}\), every coloring \(c:\kappa\times\omega\to 2\) admits sets \(A\subseteq\kappa\) and \(B\subseteq\omega\) such that \(|A|=\kappa\), \(|B|=\omega\), and \(c\restriction(A\times B)\) is constant; equivalently, \(\binom{\kappa}{\omega}\to\binom{\kappa}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) for every such \(\kappa\), including \(\kappa=\mathfrak{s}\) itself? ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting Problem 3.14 in §3 almost verbatim. The paragraph immediately before it says this is a 'slightly stronger version' of Problem 3.13, and the nearby explanation invokes Theorem 2.6 to show that below the splitting number the positive relation is already automatic at cardinals of uncountable cofinality; this explains the paper’s parenthetical emphasis on 'including \(\kappa=s\) itself.' Definition 1.1 gives the exact semantics of the arrow notation, and the sentence immediately after Problem 3.14 records the further paper-faithful constraint that any such model must have \(c<\aleph_\omega\). ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
